title: Certify when inverse signs may cross half-up rounding
body:
An admitted one-entry pinned PR628 leaf adds 1/16 at precision 4 and its unchanged inverse restores exactly. Moving the negative sign inside the last half-up rounding instead leaves 1/16. This is a source-bound counterexample to a proposed compiler rewrite, not a current source bug.

A uniform affine-domain theorem characterizes safety exactly: after expressing scaled offset and slopes as integers over D, half-grid ties exist iff D is even and gcd(D,slopes) divides D/2-offset. Complete residue oracles cover 21,316 scalar and 21,316 two-parameter domains; 285 actual leaf trials isolate 150 tie failures and 135 off-tie positive controls. All original inverse pairs restore.

Python 3.12.14 registered optimized replay and git diff checks pass. Frozen sources unchanged; no supplier or kappa claim. Credits and substantial OpenAI Codex assistance disclosed; Apache-2.0.

Base: `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`. [Coordinated research batch](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1163#discussioncomment-18922638); round 09. The selected record is unchanged.
